The poet uses humorous clues, exaggeration and playful danger to identify wild animals. The lion, tiger and leopard are presented as dangerous, while the bear hugs, the hyena laughs and the crocodile sheds tears. The contrast makes the poem funny.

The poem says physical beauty is temporary and can be changed. Anne Gregory's hair attracts people, but the poem questions whether such attraction is true love. Only God can love a person for the inner self alone, so inner beauty is valued over appearance.

Education changes Bholi from a timid, neglected girl into a confident young woman. Her teacher encourages her to speak and learn. Education gives her self-respect and the courage to reject Bishamber's dowry demand.

Lencho expected a good harvest because his crop was flourishing. The hailstorm destroyed it, bringing despair. He wrote to God for money. The postmaster collected money and sent it to preserve Lencho's faith. Lencho was relieved to receive the envelope but angry that some money was missing. Thus hope, apparent fulfilment and destruction followed one another.

The pilot began happily because he was returning home and expected breakfast with his family. The clear sky and moon made the flight pleasant. A storm then appeared, his instruments failed and he became lost. A mysterious black aeroplane guided him through the storm. After landing, he learned that no such plane had been recorded, turning pleasure into mystery and fear.

The young seagull feared that his wings would not support him. His family encouraged him by calling him and showing that the others could fly. His mother finally tempted him with food and stopped just beyond reach. Driven by hunger, he jumped and spread his wings. He discovered that he could fly and soon joined his family confidently.

Buddha teaches that life is temporary and full of suffering. Death is unavoidable. Kisa Gotami learns this when she cannot find a household untouched by death. She understands that grief is universal. Buddha advises acceptance of mortality and freedom from attachment. Peace comes through understanding this truth.

The tiger is unhappy because captivity prevents it from living naturally. It is confined to a small cage instead of roaming and hunting in the jungle. It cannot use its strength freely and hears the sounds of patrolling cars at night. The poem contrasts natural freedom with helpless confinement.

The boy learns responsibility through losing his ball. The ball has emotional value because it carries memories, so another ball cannot replace it. He must learn to accept loss and understand that possessions can disappear. This experience is a step towards maturity.

a) The constitution is a fundamental document defining the position and powers of the legislature, executive and judiciary and their relation to citizens. b) Its purpose is also to limit governmental authority so that tyranny and oppression are prevented.

Model essay: Google has become a useful online friend for students. It helps us find information, meanings, maps, images and educational resources quickly. Students can learn beyond textbooks and clarify difficult topics. It supports research and digital learning. However, every online result is not necessarily accurate, so students should compare information with reliable sources. Excessive searching can waste time and privacy and safety must also be considered. Google should be used as a learning tool, not a replacement for teachers or books. Responsible use can make learning faster, wider and more interesting. OR Model essay: Water pollution is a serious threat because all living things depend on clean water. Sewage, industrial waste, plastic and agricultural chemicals pollute rivers, lakes and groundwater. Polluted water spreads disease and harms aquatic life. We should treat waste before releasing it, avoid dumping plastic, use chemicals carefully and protect local water bodies. Saving and protecting water is everyone's responsibility. Responsible action today can ensure safe water for future generations.

Model formal letter: Shailaja/Shamit, Class X, Adarsha Vidyalaya, Kalaburgi to the Chief Engineer, GESCOM, Kalaburgi. Subject: Complaint regarding evening power cuts. Sir/Madam, I wish to draw attention to frequent evening power cuts. They disturb students' study hours and affect households. I request you to investigate the problem and ensure regular power supply, especially in the evening. Kindly take necessary action at the earliest. Yours faithfully, Shailaja/Shamit. OR Model informal letter: Vinay/Vinuta, St Joseph High School, Hasan to Grandfather. Dear Grandfather, I warmly invite you and grandmother to our Grand Parents' Day programme on [date] at [time] in the school auditorium. Your presence will make the occasion special. I hope you will attend and bless us. With love, Vinay/Vinuta.

grammar.11: In passive voice, the object becomes the subject and the doer is introduced by 'by'.
grammar.12: Remove the exclamatory form and state the idea directly as an assertive sentence.
grammar.13: Use 'too + adjective + to-infinitive' to show that a quality prevents an action.
grammar.28: A yes/no question in reported speech uses 'whether/if' and statement word order.
grammar.29: Comparative 'than any other' can become positive 'no other ... as ... as' and superlative 'the ...-est'.
grammar.30: 'Plant' is a noun when it names a living organism and a verb when it names the action of putting it in soil.

Anne came from a loving Jewish family. Her father Otto Frank was caring and understanding; her mother Edith was affectionate but sometimes strict. Anne had an elder sister, Margot. The family went into hiding during Nazi persecution. Anne was especially close to her father and used her diary to express her feelings.

The pader was an important traditional baker in Goa. He supplied bread and sweet breads for daily meals and special occasions. His bamboo staff announced his arrival. Children eagerly waited for bread-bangles. Baking was respected and the profession continued through generations.

The tiger is confined behind bars and cannot roam freely. It moves along the cage and ignores visitors. At night it hears patrolling cars instead of jungle sounds. In the wild it would stalk prey and live according to its instincts. The poem shows the sadness of captivity.

Belinda appears timid at first, but when danger comes she shows courage. She faces the pirate and calls for help. Her action contrasts humorously with the earlier boasting of the characters and shows that real courage appears in a crisis.

Matilda is unhappy because she longs for wealth, luxury and social status. She ignores the comforts she has and constantly compares her life with an imagined rich life. The story teaches that contentment is important and envy can cause suffering.

Model essay: Television can inform youth through news, educational programmes, documentaries, interviews and discussions. It can improve general knowledge and awareness. However, students should choose programmes carefully because excessive entertainment wastes time and unverified information can mislead. With moderation and guidance, television can support education and make young people aware of the world. OR Model essay: Natural resources such as water, forests, soil, minerals and wildlife are essential. Pollution, deforestation and overuse are damaging them. We should plant trees, conserve water, recycle, use renewable energy and enforce environmental laws. Students can save water and avoid waste. Restoring resources is a responsibility towards future generations.

The hailstorm destroyed Lencho's entire crop. It beat down the corn and flowers and covered the field with ice. The plants were ruined as if cut with a knife. The year's harvest was completely lost, leaving Lencho without food or income and driving him to ask God for help.

Mandela fought apartheid, the system of racial discrimination in South Africa. He joined the struggle for equal rights and made many sacrifices, including imprisonment. He never abandoned the cause of freedom and later supported reconciliation. His struggle helped bring democratic government and equality.

The crow and hemlock tree are linked with unpleasant images, yet the snow they shake onto the poet changes his mood. The incident refreshes him and removes some regret. Something apparently negative therefore produces a positive effect.

The poet uses humour, exaggeration and playful danger to identify animals. The lion, tiger and leopard are dangerous in comic ways, while the bear hugs, the hyena laughs and the crocodile cries. These clues turn the poem into a humorous guessing game.

Hari Singh gradually understands the value of education. After stealing Anil's money, he realises that education can give him a better future than crime. He returns the money because he does not want to lose Anil's trust or his chance to learn.

The Proposal is quarrelsome because Lomov and Natalya argue over Oxen Meadows and their dogs, while Chubukov joins the insults. Even a marriage proposal becomes a series of accusations. OR Valli's enthusiasm is dampened when she sees the dead cow that had earlier run happily beside the bus. The sight makes her think about the sadness and uncertainty of life.

The phrase refers to the tiger in A Tiger in the Zoo. His natural strength is trapped behind bars instead of being used freely in the jungle.
The line is from The Ball Poem. The ball is cheap and replaceable materially, but it has emotional value because of the boy's memories and his first experience of loss.

His curiosity and energetic behaviour make the journey chaotic and memorable. Coorg is called a piece of heaven because it has green hills, evergreen forests, coffee plantations, streams, wildlife and the Brahmagiri hills. Its pleasant climate and scenic landscape make it beautiful and attractive to visitors. OR Buddha teaches that life involves suffering, change and death. Attachment causes sorrow, death is unavoidable and people should accept mortality and overcome attachment to find peace.

The Trees presents nature struggling to escape human confinement. The trees seem to move out of the house towards the forest, which represents freedom. The poem suggests that nature cannot be permanently controlled. OR It is unfair to judge people only by appearance. For Anne Gregory shows that physical beauty can attract people but may not be true love; inner qualities matter more, and only God can love purely for the inner self.

Model essay: Plastic is useful but uncontrolled use has become a major environmental problem. Single-use plastic pollutes land and water, remains for a long time and harms animals. Burning it can release harmful substances. We should reduce single-use plastic, use reusable alternatives, separate waste and recycle. Schools and communities can spread awareness and governments can enforce rules. Responsible choices can protect the environment. OR Model essay: Good manners make a person respectful, pleasant and responsible. Polite speech, listening, patience, honesty, cleanliness and consideration for others are important. Good manners help people live peacefully at home, school and in public. True manners should be shown to everyone, not only important people. Good behaviour builds trust and friendship and makes education meaningful.

grammar.1: 'Last night' indicates simple past, so 'blew' is correct.
grammar.2: Positive simple-present statement with 'grows' takes the negative tag 'doesn't he?'.
grammar.3: The word 'like' makes the comparison a simile.
grammar.4: Use 'a' before the consonant sound in 'bachelor's' and 'the' for the specific university name.
grammar.6: 'Reach out to' means make contact with.
grammar.8: Add the negative prefix to form 'unnoble'.
grammar.11: Past continuous passive uses 'was/were + being + past participle'.
grammar.12: For the underlined phrase 'in reading books', frame a WH-question with correct auxiliary order.
grammar.13: An exclamatory sentence can use 'How + adverb + subject + verb!'.
grammar.28: 'One of the most...' can be changed to 'more ... than most other' and 'very few ... as ... as'.
grammar.29: 'As soon as' links the first event; 'No sooner' requires inversion and 'than'.
grammar.30: A reported yes/no question uses 'whether/if', statement order and backshift where appropriate.
